faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary for a teaching job in Victoria?

faqs.q: Does the vic teacher salary include casual loading or super?

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay: A Guide for Victorian Teachers

If you're a teacher in Victoria or considering a teaching role, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual pay is essential. Whether you're comparing a salary offer or calculating your take-home pay, the formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This article explains the conversion, highlights state differences in ordinary-time earnings, and covers key Australian pay concepts like the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and superannuation.

### The Basic Formula and Assumptions

To estimate your annual gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the standard is 38 hours per week under the Fair Work Act. For example:

- $40 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $79,040 per year

If you work part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – use the checkbox instead.

### State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026), full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Victoria are $2,041.1 per week. This is slightly below the national average of $2,083.7 per week. These figures are averages across all occupations and industries, not a median for any specific job. For a **vic teacher salary**, actual pay depends on the relevant award or enterprise agreement, such as the Victorian Government Schools Agreement. Teacher salaries are typically set by classification level and years of experience, not by a market median.

### Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.9 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, most teachers are covered by awards that set higher minimum rates. For example, a graduate teacher in Victoria may start at a rate above the minimum. Casual teachers (relief or supply) are entitled to the 25% loading on top of their base award rate. Always check the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) for your specific classification.

### Fortnightly Pay and Tax

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the example above: $79,040 per year ÷ 26 fortnights = $3,040 per fortnight (before tax). Tax is withheld using the 2026–27 resident tax scale:

- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a detailed estimate.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee at 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. For a teacher earning $79,040, that's an extra $9,484.80 per year (up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base). Super is not deducted from your pay – it's an additional cost to the employer. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary packaging can affect your super.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Using the Calculator

To get a personalised estimate, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate. If you're a casual teacher, check the casual loading box (adds 25%). The calculator will show your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. For reference tables on award rates and average earnings, see our [reference tables](/data).
